title: Compliance Director, Trust Company and Custody Operations
description: Vestwell is the financial technology company powering the new savings economy. The New York City-based fintech platform redefines how people save for the critical aspects of life across retirement, education, and healthcare savings needs. Today, Vestwell enables over 790,000 businesses and more than 2.75 million active savers, with over $57 billion in assets saved across all 50 United States.  Vestwell offers a range of products, including workplace-delivered retirement plans, employer-offered student loan repayment benefits, and various savings accounts for education, emergencies, and individuals with disabilities. Vestwell's platform serves a diverse clientele, including financial advisers, employers, third-party administrators, financial institutions, payroll providers, government agencies, and individual savers. To learn more, visit  vestwell.com Who Are We Looking For? We are seeking an experienced and strategic Compliance Director of Trust Company and Custody Operations to lead and manage regulatory compliance and operational oversight across our trust company, custodial, and trading operations. This individual will play a key role in ensuring compliance with all applicable regulations related to 401(k) plans, ERISA, and trust and custody services. The ideal candidate will bring a deep understanding of regulatory requirements, operational excellence, and a proven track record in managing regulatory operations within financial services or trust company and retirement plan administration. What Will You Be Doing? Lead the regulatory operations function with a focus on qualified retirement plans , particularly 401(k) plans, IRAs, and Emergency Savings Accounts. Create and implement procedures and internal controls for all trading activities within our custodial operations and proactively monitor our teams and systems for compliance with applicable laws and regulations.   Ensure compliance with ERISA , Internal Revenue Code (IRC) , DOL , IRS , trust company regulations, and SEC regulations. Oversee and enhance controls related to trust and custody operations, as well as state savings programs , ensuring alignment with fiduciary standards and regulatory expectations. Provide regular reporting to internal stakeholders and Risk Committee about material risks, incidents, and the effectiveness of risk mitigation strategies.  Partner with internal stakeholders (legal, compliance, product, operations) to interpret new and existing regulations and apply them to business practices. Monitor regulatory developments and proactively advise senior leadership on potential business impacts and required changes. Serve as the lead for  the Legal Team to lead the Vestwell Trust Company SOC 1 audit and New Hampshire Banking Department regulatory exam.  Liaise with external auditors, regulatory agencies, and third-party service providers during examinations, audits, inquiries, or other matters as needed.  Oversee and support regulatory reporting and filings (e.g., Form 5500, IRS/DOL disclosures). Manage a team of regulatory operations professionals, providing leadership, coaching, and performance oversight. Drive continuous improvement and automation of regulatory and compliance processes and controls. Requirements The Necessities Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or a related field required; advanced degree or professional certification (e.g., JD, CPA, CRSP, QKA, CISP) preferred. Minimum of 10+ years of experience with a proven track record in regulatory compliance or operations in the retirement, trust, or custodial services industry. Deep knowledge of ERISA, 401(k) regulations, trust company laws, custody services, and applicable IRS/DOL regulations. Experience managing operational risk, compliance audits, and regulatory examinations. Strong leadership and team management skills with the ability to influence and collaborate across functions. Exceptional organizational, analytical, and communication skills. Experience working with recordkeeping platforms, trust accounting systems, or custodial platforms is a plus. The Extras Start up experience This role will be based in the New York City office, and will be part of Vestwell's hybrid in-office operation. The expected base salary range for this position is $160K - $180K base. This position is eligible to participate in the Company Bonus Pool and is eligible to receive new hire equity in the Company. Please note that salary bands are based on NY and other similar metro areas and may differ based on where the role is ultimately hired. Employee Benefits We’re an innovative, high-growth company with an exciting future ahead. At Vestwell, we prioritize employee wellbeing through comprehensive health benefits, generous time off, and a dedicated Employee Wellbeing Committee. Engagements will encompass a broad range of credit risk-related matters and may include the following: credit risk review or loan review work, credit administration and policy review, quality assurance/ internal audits of loan review departments, and other credit risk specific engagements. Key responsibilities include: Lead and Inspire: Manage and mentor multidisciplinary teams, fostering a collaborative, client-focused culture that delivers exceptional results. Deliver Expertise: Provide deep subject-matter knowledge in credit risk mitigation, credit policies, and procedures across a variety of engagements. Drive Excellence: Oversee credit risk reviews, loan reviews, internal audits, and policy assessments with precision and strategic insight. Client Engagement: Communicate industry trends and best practices effectively to clients, offering actionable recommendations and thought leadership. Practice Development: Contribute to internal initiatives including talent development, business growth, and service innovation. Mentorship & Talent Growth: Support the professional development of team members through coaching, feedback, and career guidance. Market Presence: Build your personal brand and network to identify new opportunities and drive growth for the risk consulting practice. This order of magnitude increase in speed is transforming the user experience of AI applications, unlocking real-time iteration and increasing intelligence via additional agentic computation. Cerebras works with the leading model labs, global enterprises, and cutting-edge AI-native startups. OpenAI recently announced a multi-year partnership https://openai.com/index/cerebras-partnership/ with Cerebras, to deploy 750 megawatts of scale, transforming key workloads with ultra high-speed inference. We build the compiler frontend, model transformation pipeline, graph optimization infrastructure, high-performance kernel enablement, and runtime integration that together make next-generation AI models execute with industry-leading performance. The team works at the intersection of machine learning frameworks, compiler technologies, distributed systems, hardware architecture, and model optimization. You will lead the engineering organization responsible for ML model compilation and optimization as well as development of high-performance kernels. This role combines deep technical leadership with organizational excellence. You will partner across compiler, runtime, cloud infrastructure, hardware architecture, product management, and AI research teams while helping shape the future of AI inference at Cerebras. Delivery & Execution - Own planning, prioritization, and execution across multiple concurrent initiatives. - Balance rapid model support with long-term ML Compiler architecture. - Drive predictable delivery for strategic customer commitments. Preferred Qualifications - Experience building compiler frontends for AI accelerators. - Experience supporting PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, or ONNX. - Experience with LLM inference or training systems. - Familiarity with distributed compilation. - Experience working with hardware architects. - Experience leading teams through rapid growth. title: Product Policy Manager, Product Risk
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Team As the Product Policy Manager for Product Risk, you will play a crucial role in setting and executing the Safeguards team’s approach to assessing product launches for safety risks and working with XFN stakeholders to drive appropriate safety mitigations. You'll work closely with a suite of cross-functional teams, within and outside of Safeguards, including, product, legal, public policy, and engineering teams to understand upcoming features, anticipate potential misuses or unintended consequences, and craft policies that balance innovation with responsibility. Your work will be essential in maintaining Anthropic's commitment to safe and beneficial AI as we continue to expand our product capabilities. IMPORTANT CONTEXT ON THIS ROLE: In this position you may be exposed to and engage with explicit content spanning a range of topics, including those of a sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing nature.  Responsibilities: Develop and maintain risk assessment frameworks to identify and evaluate potential safety risks associated with new product features and functionality Conduct and drive comprehensive product safety reviews, covering technical and non technical harms, to inform product launch and safety mitigation strategies  Collaborate closely with a variety of stakeholders including product and engineering teams and the broader Safeguards team to leverage deep policy, enforcement, and engineering expertise Analyze the potential for misuse, unintended consequences, and harmful outputs of new model and product capabilities and translate this analysis into mitigations delivery. Leverage SME risk assessments to inform overall product safety recommendations Design and run bespoke evaluations for products that require tailored assessment and contribute to our product safety evaluations strategy.  Craft policy recommendations that strike a balance between enabling innovation and ensuring responsible AI deployment Stay current on industry trends and emerging risks in AI development to proactively address potential issues Contribute to regular reports on product policy risks and mitigations for senior leadership Minimum Requirements: Have a strong technical background while also feeling equally comfortable explaining highly technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders Understand safety policies and safety considerations associated with a wide range of product surfaces  Are adept at prioritizing where, and how, to focus resources for safety mitigations in a high volume launch process Have conducted risk evaluations of novel products in fast moving organizations  Demonstrated expertise collaborating with product and engineering teams to integrate safety considerations into product development Have a thorough understanding of AI ethics, responsible AI principles, and current debates surrounding AI safety and governance Have the ability to think creatively about potential misuses of technology and develop innovative solutions to mitigate risks Have shown strong program management skills with the ability to drive policy development processes from ideation to implementation The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.  For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.
